plan: Plans three vegetarian, high-protein weeknight dinners; asks for recipes without cilantro because she can't stand it.

messages.text: Hi! Need some help planning dinners for the week.
Hi Maya! Happy to help with your weekly meal planning. What kind of meals are you looking for today?
Looking for three vegetarian, high-protein weeknight dinners. And please, no cilantro in any recipes!
Got it, Maya! Three vegetarian, high-protein dinners, no cilantro, perfect for your family. How about a hearty Lentil Shepherd's Pie for your first meal? It's packed with protein.
Sounds good! What's another option?
Great! For your second meal, a Black Bean and Corn Stuffed Bell Peppers recipe is a good choice. It's high in protein and easy to prepare without cilantro.
Perfect. One more, please.
Certainly! How about a Tofu Scramble with Roasted Sweet Potatoes and Spinach? It's quick, protein-rich, and works well for a weeknight dinner for your family.
Awesome, thanks! I'll add these to my pickup order.
You're welcome, Maya! Let me know if you need any adjustments or more ideas for your family's pickup order.

For lunchboxes, Kroger brand applesauce pouches or individual yogurt cups are popular and economical. Making a big batch of popcorn from kernels is also a very cheap and fun snack.

plan: Mentions her doctor said her cholesterol is high and asks for heart-healthy breakfast ideas.

messages.text: Hi! Planning my pickup order for Sunday. Need some help with breakfast ideas.
Hi Maya! Happy to help with your Sunday pickup order. What kind of breakfast ideas are you looking for today?
My doctor said my cholesterol is high, so I need some heart-healthy options. Something the kids (8 & 11) might actually eat too!

Oh, I understand! We can definitely find some great heart-healthy breakfast options that your family of four will enjoy. How about starting with oatmeal with berries and nuts, or whole-wheat toast with avocado?
Oatmeal sounds good. Any specific brands or toppings you recommend that are good for cholesterol?

For oatmeal, look for rolled oats or steel-cut oats, as they're high in soluble fiber. Toppings like fresh or frozen berries, a sprinkle of chia seeds or flax seeds, and a few walnuts are excellent for heart health.
Okay, I'll add those. What about something quick for busy mornings?

For quick, heart-healthy options, you could try making a batch of overnight oats on Sunday, or grab some low-fat Greek yogurt to pair with fruit and a sprinkle of granola. Whole-wheat English muffins with a poached egg are also fast!
Perfect, thanks! I'll add some of these to my list. Appreciate the help!
You're very welcome, Maya! Let me know if you need anything else for your Sunday pickup. Have a great day!
